candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — fall prevention
candidate.educational_objective: Incorporate proactive toileting assistance into purposeful rounding for hospitalized clients at risk for falls.

options.A: Ask whether the client needs to use the bathroom and provide assistance as needed.
options.B: Substantially restrict fluids to eliminate nighttime bathroom trips.
options.C: Use toileting assistance as the only fall-prevention intervention.
options.D: Avoid asking about elimination needs because toileting is unrelated to fall prevention.

candidate.rationale: AHRQ's fall-prevention toolkit describes purposeful rounding as including standard elements such as asking whether the patient needs to go to the bathroom and checking the environment. Addressing toileting needs proactively can reduce unassisted attempts to reach the bathroom, but it is one component of a broader individualized fall-prevention plan. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Purposeful rounding for fall prevention includes proactively asking about bathroom needs and assisting with toileting as appropriate.
candidate.source_document_title: Preventing Falls in Hospitals — Falls Prevention Toolkit Webinar Transcript
